title: Controlled entry into force
effort: Turn a quiet, short entry into a purposeful upward or forward leg push.
quality_marker: In E1 record whether the two walking foot placements lead to a stable two-foot plant, clear upward push and a 2 s held reception. A rushed plant, extra hop or unstable reception consumes the attempt and triggers a simpler remaining prescription. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: Four walk-in vertical takeoffs anchor the day; two short forward takeoffs change output direction. Grounded lunge return, a stepped leg-driven release, a small step reversal and hip-finish reversal train controlled entry without adding hard approaches. Strength work is reduced while entry constraints change.

explosive.name: Walk-In Vertical Jump — step-close takeoff
explosive.job: Main conversion of a slow forward entry into an organized upward two-foot push.
explosive.cue: Take one quiet walking step, bring the second foot alongside, then use a comfortable dip and jump upward; land on two feet and hold 2 s. Exactly two entry foot placements per attempt, no run or preparatory hop.
explosive.replacement: a stationary countermovement vertical jump at the same remaining dose if the entry disrupts plant or receiving control; log removed entry steps
explosive.identity: Proposed walking step-close execution; countermovement-jump parent
explosive.novelty_reason: Introduces low-speed entry-to-vertical force rather than simply increasing height. A fast approach was rejected because entry control, not speed tolerance, is the job.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; 15 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Walk-In Broad Jump — step-close forward takeoff
explosive.key: Walk-In Broad Jump — step-close forward takeoff
explosive.job: Direct the same modest entry into a short forward leg projection.
explosive.cue: Take one quiet walking step and close the other foot, then make one modest two-foot forward jump; hold the two-foot landing 2 s. No running, added hop or distance target.
explosive.replacement: a stationary broad jump at the same remaining dose if the entry or total travel cannot fit; log removed entry steps
explosive.identity: Proposed walking step-close execution; standing-broad-jump parent
explosive.novelty_reason: Tests a different output direction with only two attempts after the vertical anchor. It is not a new family or a directly comparable distance test.
explosive.rest_text: 15 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Forward Lunge — rapid return to the starting foot line
explosive.key: Forward Lunge — rapid return to the starting foot line
explosive.job: Accept a controlled forward step and drive the front leg to regain the start.
explosive.cue: Bodyweight: step forward gently, lower under control, then push through the front whole foot to return quickly beside the other foot. Stay grounded, trunk quiet and knee aligned. Two complete returns per moving leg.
explosive.replacement: a supported stationary split-squat rapid rise at the same per-leg dose if the forward entry cannot stay controlled
explosive.identity: Proposed rapid bodyweight forward-lunge return execution
explosive.novelty_reason: Loads the front leg after a forward entry, unlike the earlier rear-step return. It practices entry-to-force without a ballistic receiving contact.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — walk-step forward release
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — walk-step forward release
explosive.job: Transfer a controlled forward step through the planted leg into a straight release.
explosive.cue: Start standing with a light ball and long arms. Take one short forward walking step, let the rear foot remain grounded in split stance, then drive legs/hips to release forward. One throw per lead leg; no airborne takeoff, torso twist or catch.
explosive.replacement: one rapid supported split-stance hip-hinge return per lead leg with no ball, using the same side recovery, if release containment fails
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-scoop-toss family; single walking-step release proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Adds controlled entry to the fixed split stance of Week 3, at two total releases. A hard run-up or chest pass would shift the problem away from grounded leg force.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 2 total reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Step-Down to Step-Up — quick grounded reversal
explosive.key: Step-Down to Step-Up — quick grounded reversal
explosive.job: Accept a small controlled lowering then push through the lead foot without flight.
explosive.cue: Stand with both feet on a low inspected step. Keep the lead foot planted, lower the other heel to a light floor touch in 2 s, then drive back up quickly until both feet join. Two complete down-and-up reps per lead leg. Do not bounce from the floor foot.
explosive.replacement: a shallow supported single-leg squat lower-and-rise at the same per-leg dose if the step height or path is unsuitable
explosive.identity: step-up parent; controlled heel-touch reversal proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Adds a controlled lowering-to-drive transition to the earlier grounded step-up start. It is one continuous step exercise, not a step-down plus another exercise.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Glute Bridge — controlled lower to rapid reversal
explosive.key: Glute Bridge — controlled lower to rapid reversal
explosive.job: Express hip-finish force after a controlled loaded-position change.
explosive.cue: Bodyweight, begin in a level bilateral bridge; lower for 2 s until the pelvis lightly meets the floor, then rise rapidly without pausing or arching. Four continuous reps, settling on the floor after the final return.
explosive.replacement: four floor-start bridge rises with 10 s full resets and the same 90 s transition if the reversal causes cramp or lumbar compensation; record the extra actual reset time
explosive.identity: bodyweight-glute-bridge parent; continuous rapid reversal proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: The controlled return replaces the settled floor start, giving a grounded hip-force counterpart to entry-to-push. No new unstable support is needed.

resilience.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction — light
resilience.job: Light medial-hip force to maintain a straight stance-leg push without drifting away from the foot.
resilience.cue: Top foot rests in front of the lower knee. Lift the straight lower leg slightly 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; pelvis remains stacked.
resilience.replacement: a smaller controlled lower-leg lift at the same dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 45 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Tibialis Raise — wall-supported
resilience.job: Light ankle dorsiflexor loading to control foot position before a stable push/landing.
resilience.cue: Back against an inspected wall, heels on floor; lift forefeet 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Adjust foot distance to stay easy.
resilience.replacement: a seated unweighted toe raise through comfortable range
resilience.identity: Verified family: tibialis-raise; wall-supported execution declared

primary.cue: Step back quietly, lower under control and push through the whole front foot to stand; about 4 s per complete cycle. Do not launch off the trailing toes.
primary.replacement: a stationary split squat at the same per-leg dose if stepping reduces control

primary.cue: Start in a bilateral bridge. Each cycle is two small heel steps out per foot, then two back per foot: eight placements in about 8 s. Keep a soft knee and level hips; never chase a fully straight leg.
primary.replacement: a shorter-lever walkout at the same complete-cycle count; reduce range for sagging or cramp and stop if control does not return

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: Mark the whole walking entry and takeoff/receiving corridor within the first 3 m, leaving 7 m clear; shorten steps and projection or use stationary replacements if the actual athlete cannot fit. E1/E2 contain 12 total walking entry foot placements and E4 adds two, for 14 prescribed approach steps. Ordinary reset walks and grounded lunge/step movements are separate unmeasured travel, not sprint metres or jump contacts. No start is outside the lane. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 53–60 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: Week 8 had seven primary rounds/seven bilateral bouts. Here Reverse Lunge returns at 1 × 4 per leg, RDL falls 2 × 5 to 1 × 5 and Goblet Squat stays 1 × 5; bridge gives way to the lead-leg job. Six rounds/seven bouts contain 30 conventional reps plus two cycles. Keep all approach entries walking-speed, and hold load while actual entry control is assessed; no faster entry or heavier load follows automatically.
audit_findings: Six bilateral landings, two grounded throws and 14 walking approach steps are separate prescribed events. No approach is a sprint and no initial hop/drop is concealed. All six changed executions are related variants, not claims of six unrelated inventions. Two takeoff vectors have different jobs with unequal doses, while the grounded supports limit additional receiving exposure.
